title: Including link endpoints raised two-link detection bounds in two partial adult worm circuit models
abstract: We tested whether a 24-cell response panel can distinguish two changed electrical links from one in passive models of two partial adult worm maps. We sampled 300 link pairs per map and ten random panels per pair. We formed paired panels that included all changed-link endpoints. Both links doubled. At leak equal to mean positive weighted degree and independent known Gaussian noise of 1 percent of baseline panel RMS per entry and condition, 73.4 and 64.7 percent of endpoint panels met a sufficient condition for at least 99 percent detection power. Random panel shares were 0.93 and 0.33 percent. Pair bootstrap intervals for the gains were 67.67 to 77.13 and 59.37 to 69.27 percentage points. These intervals describe model sampling, not animal variation. The test uses a standard low-rank inverse identity and a Gaussian operator-noise bound. At tenfold leak the endpoint shares fell below 0.7 percent. Partial annotation, assumed conductance and leak, known endpoint locations, self-response access, and no matched activity limit biological use. Original code, aggregate results, figures, source hashes and separate external-data retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: The share of 24-cell panels that met a sufficient condition for at least 99 percent detection power for two link doublings depends on endpoint access, leak and assumed noise. Shares are model results on two fixed partial adult worm maps.

citations.reason: Prior one-link remote-response study documents the source and cell selection. We test two-link detection and panel design with new code.
